nodes.description: CHK2 is activated by ATM after a double-strand break and phosphorylates BRCA1, BRCA2, p53 and CDC25 to initiate repair, apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest. Reduced CHK2 function attenuates that signal. The extent to which this translates into a failed p53 checkpoint is disputed - CHK2's contribution to activating p53-dependent arrest has been described as dispensable - so the node is curated as an attenuated signal rather than as checkpoint abolition.

nodes.description: In most CHEK2-associated breast cancers the second allele is lost, so the germline variant acts as a first hit and the tumour is CHEK2-null. Unlike BRCA1- and BRCA2-driven tumours, these cancers do not show a homologous recombination deficiency signature, which is one reason the downstream oncogenic mechanism is still unsettled.

nodes.description: Female breast cancer is the predominant tumour. Reported lifetime risk ranges from 20% to 44% depending on family history. Tumours are typically oestrogen receptor positive invasive ductal carcinoma of no special type, luminal B, and arise in younger women with higher rates of multifocal and bilateral disease.
